body: The wording implies `npm run test:track` requires the dev server to be on the default port, but the harness supports `--url` (and `npm run test:track -- --url ...`) to target a different instance. Rephrase to avoid the contradiction and to show the recommended override invocation.

This section makes a definitive legal/attribution claim (“no external attribution requirement”) without pointing to any license/terms for the Google sample videos. Since this file is the repo’s source-of-truth for license/attribution expectations, it’s safer to avoid an unverified legal assertion and instead state the intended usage + that upstream terms should be checked before redistribution.

`config/cctv_sources.austin.json` is currently an empty array, so calling it a “reference live pack” (and suggesting readers “see either file” for the schema) is misleading. The live Austin catalog is loaded from open-data when file/env packs are empty; the Shinjuku file is the only on-disk example schema here.

`stop({ squelch: true })` only plays a squelch burst when the prior state was `'playing'`. That makes calls like `toggleAudio()`’s “no stream URL” branch (and any stop while connecting/error) silently skip the intended squelch feedback.

`setAutoTune(false)` currently only flips the flag; because `resolveAtcTune()` doesn’t use its `autoTune` param, the AUTO toggle won’t actually stop station/frequency from continuing to auto-resolve. A simple way to make the toggle effective is to snapshot the current tune into `manualAirportIcao` / `manualFreqType` when disabling, and clear those overrides when re-enabling.

PR description says auto-tuning engages within 50 NM, but `DEFAULT_ATC_RANGE_M` is set to ~35 NM (64820 m). Either the implementation or the description needs to change; if 50 NM is intended, update the constant accordingly.
The new `.atc-radio-card` uses `backdrop-filter` but omits the `-webkit-backdrop-filter` fallback that’s used elsewhere in `style.css`, which can cause the glass effect to disappear in Safari/WebKit.

NeoWs records intentionally publish `lat`/`lon` as null, while `analystEngine` defaults an omitted scope to `{ kind: 'view' }` and filters null-coordinate records out of view/radius/region scopes. With this layer now advertised, a normal request such as “how many asteroids?” can return zero unless the model explicitly supplies `scope.kind: 'anywhere'`; add NEO-specific anywhere guidance here or make the query default handle non-spatial layers.

This adds `NEO_API_KEY` to the documented provider configuration, but it is not registered in `KEY_SETUP_KEYS`/`knownKeySetupEnvVars` (unlike the existing FIRMS, TomTom, AIS, and Launch Library server-side keys). Consequently Provider Settings and `/api/setup` reject this key as unknown, leaving users with only manual `.env` editing despite the app's central key setup flow; register a NeoWs entry or explicitly document that it is manual-only.

Although this registry exposes the NEO numeric/flag fields, `runAnalystQuery()` later compacts result items using a hard-coded allow-list that omits `sizeM`, `missKm`, `missLunar`, `velocityKph`, `absMag`, and `hazardous`. Voice queries can filter/sort on these fields internally but the returned items give the model none of their values, so it cannot narrate the requested asteroid attributes; add the NEO fields to that payload and cover the voice seam.

Returning `false` here makes the standard DataLayerManager treat the initial enable as a lifecycle rejection (`_doToggle` checks `updated === false`) and immediately call `disable()`. A keyless user therefore cannot leave this layer enabled with the promised `KEY REQUIRED` chip (and voice enable reports failure), unlike the FIRMS `no_key` path; return a non-false handled result here and cover the manager path in a test.

Adding the NEO layer here is not enough for the voice tool to generate NEO queries: the `filters` description at line 6388 still lists only the pre-existing fields and omits `sizeM`, `missKm`, `missLunar`, `velocityKph`, `absMag`, `hazardous`, and `name`. Since the model relies on that vocabulary, requests such as hazardous or >500 m asteroids won't be formed even though `ANALYST_LAYERS` accepts them. Add the NEO fields to that description.

The PR specifies a smoothing alpha of 0.08, but this uses 0.1 (`0.9/0.1`). That changes the documented smoothing behavior and cap reaction timing; use the stated 0.92/0.08 weighting.

This starts the neighbor queue but never marks the documented 95% `prewarming road grid` phase; both callers set the phase to 100 before invoking it, and `getStats()` forces 100 once `_fetching` ends. Thus the queue-depth busy state can only display 100% with fallback text, never the promised prewarm phase. Set 95%/the prewarm label while `_prewarming` is active and transition to 100% when the queue drains.

- line 1278

`prioritizedRoads` is only an ordering, but `allocateRoadDotBudgets` calculates the complete budget for all roads before the spawn loop and its fairness pass sorts by ideal dot count rather than this order. When the cap is exceeded, viewport/intersection status therefore does not make central roads claim dots first, so this mitigation does not change the budget distribution; make the allocator priority-aware instead.

The PR specifies 250-dot decrements, but the default here is 300 and the runtime does not override `stepDown`, so each degradation changes the cap in 300-dot increments. Use 250 to match the stated adaptive-cap contract.

Although `fineStepSec` remains a documented parameter, it is unused here and the adapter never forwards it; `findNextSatellitePass` hard-codes 10-second sampling. Existing callers that set this legacy cadence therefore silently get different peak/LOS results, contradicting the claimed backward compatibility. Please pass the option through to the new engine, or remove it and explicitly document the behavioral break.

This interpolation calls `lookAnglesAt` at the left sample, and the matching right call below, after the transit loop has already propagated through the pass. That adds two SGP4 propagations per candidate pass, so the implementation does not meet the PR's stated zero-additional-call refinement; retain adjacent transit samples while scanning if that guarantee is required, or correct the stated performance contract.

Allowing `visiblePass` to be null makes this test pass when `requireVisible` rejects every pass in the 72-hour window, so it does not verify that the filter can find or return a visible pass. Assert that a pass is present before checking its visibility and ordering.

This assertion exercises only an empty catalog, so it returns `no-tle` before either `Number(noradId)` or the new successful lookup/delegation path runs. A regression that removes string coercion or breaks pass prediction would still pass this test; populate a catalog with a valid satrec and assert the coerced ID reaches an `ok` result, while keeping the cold/invalid cases separate.
Fixed: the test now asserts `visiblePass` exists before checking `visible`.

Populated the catalog with a valid satrec using `_setTrackedSatelliteRefreshStateForTest` and verified that both numeric NORAD ID `25544` and string `'25544'` successfully return status `'ok'` with the pass payload, while preserving separate assertions for cold and non-existent IDs.

Added `fineStepSec` to `findNextSatellitePass` options (defaulting to 5s, configurable down to 1s) and forwarded it directly from `findNextIssPass`, preserving legacy cadence behavior with dedicated unit test coverage.
Fixed: the peak fit reuses the neighbouring transit samples, so it adds no extra propagations.

This registration increases the catalog from 19 to 20 layers, but `src/app/constructCatalog.test.mjs:41` still asserts `first.layers.length === 19`. The catalog test therefore fails on every run; update that expected count (and any related catalog-count assertions) with this addition.

Adding `meteors` makes `REGISTERED_LAYER_IDS` contain 20 entries, but `src/data/layerState.test.mjs:161-162` still asserts a registry length and unique-count of 19. That production registry test will fail until both expectations are updated for the new shareable layer.

The empty-snapshot branch does not validate the envelope's empty invariants: `{ records: [], totalCount: -1, timeFrom: 123, timeTo: 0, ... }` passes because the time checks only run when records exist. Since this validator is the guard before replacing the displayed batch, malformed empty responses can be accepted and surfaced as valid data; require an empty batch to have `totalCount === 0` and both bounds `null`.

When the first acquisition fails, `refresh()` sets `retryAfter` and this branch marks the request failed; because `cache` is still null, line 51 then throws on every toggle until the 60-second cooldown expires. That contradicts the panel's “Toggle this layer to try again” recovery path (and the QA interception bypasses this provider behavior). Please make an explicit user retry bypass the cooldown, or change the UI/docs to expose the wait.

I think this PR would benefit from making the contract of `geoDistance.js` explicit before it becomes the shared implementation for all of these consumers.

The current API is:

```js
greatCircleKm(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2)
```

The positional `(lat, lon)` convention is documented, but it is still structurally possible to pass `(lon, lat)` and receive a finite, plausible-looking distance, which is particularly relevant because #274 was opened around exactly that class of silent coordinate-order error.

Could we settle and document the following as part of this PR/#274 coordination?

* the canonical coordinate representation and whether a point-object form should be preferred for shared/public spatial APIs;
* canonical units and the relationship between `greatCircleKm` / `greatCircleMeters`;
* explicit behavior for `NaN`, `Infinity`, missing coordinates, and out-of-range latitude/longitude;
* whether `greatCircleKm` is the sole canonical name, with the existing `haversineKm` exports only retained temporarily for compatibility where necessary.

I think getting this contract right now will prevent the repository from replacing duplicated implementations with a duplicated ambiguity.

Since this PR makes `geoDistance.js` the shared implementation for a large number of existing consumers, I think the dedicated test should establish the core invariants more comprehensively.

The current tests cover the basic calculation, but I would add explicit cases for:

```text
identity
symmetry: d(a,b) === d(b,a)
one-degree calibration
dateline crossing
antipodal points
non-finite / invalid coordinates
explicit latitude-before-longitude regression
```

I’d also add a small number of consumer-level regression checks for code paths where the distance is used as a threshold or selection criterion.

In particular, the Natural Earth migration is worth locking down with a regression case because the previous implementation used `(lon, lat, lon, lat)` while the new shared contract is `(lat, lon, lat, lon)`.

That would give us confidence in both halves of the refactor:

```text
canonical distance function is correct
+
existing consumer semantics remain correct
```

rather than only demonstrating that the new helper produces plausible distances.

Addressed in 9c638fa. The canonical shared API is now object-based: `greatCircleKm({ lat, lon }, { lat, lon })`, with `greatCircleMeters` as the exact metre conversion. The helper validates finite WGS84-style ranges and returns `Infinity` for missing, non-finite, or out-of-range points so invalid data is excluded from threshold and nearest-item selections. It uses the IUGG mean radius (6371.0088 km), preserving the prior voice-path value. Existing exported `haversineKm` entry points remain only as compatibility wrappers that delegate to the canonical helper.

I rebuilt the change on current `main` because several consumers moved during the intervening refactors, and migrated the new module locations as part of that refresh.

Addressed in 9c638fa. The dedicated tests now cover identity, symmetry, one-degree calibration, dateline crossing, antipodal points, metre conversion, non-finite/missing/out-of-range inputs, explicit point-key shape, and a latitude/longitude swap regression.

I also added consumer regressions for the Natural Earth `[lon, lat]` bbox conversion, route plausibility invalid-position fallback, and traffic fetch-center threshold/fallback behavior. Verification on current `main`: 4,142 tests passed with one expected platform skip; 273 focused consumer tests passed; package/import boundaries passed; formatting passed; production build passed.

Removing these subscriptions in `disable()` makes the first toggle off permanent: `init()` installs them only once, while `enable()` never re-adds them. After disable→enable, camera moves no longer schedule loads and selected anchors stop updating. Re-register both callbacks in `enable()` (or keep teardown only in `destroy()`) before clearing them here.

The timed parser has the same fallback problem as `model.js`: rejecting the sample leaves `baseHeight` at 0, so roads above ellipsoid height can remain below the loaded terrain. Please use the same resolved-surface fallback/defer behavior here as in the production parser, not just the same numeric guard.

Please add a runtime regression test for this branch: a finite −16800 m sample should not propagate that height, while a valid sample should be retained. The existing `trafficTiming.test.mjs` assertion only compares the two parser bodies, so it would pass if both parsers used the wrong bound or fallback and cannot prevent #656 from regressing.

This issue also appears on line 61 of the same file.

Adding this fifth upstream changes runtime/provider behavior, but the required documentation is not updated: `CONTRIBUTING.md:86` requires `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` in the same PR, and CURRENT-STATE still says the proxy uses four public mirrors. Please add entries for the new mirror and the traffic/ALPR fixes before merging.

This issue also appears on line 26 of the same file.

`Number('')` evaluates to `0`, so a malformed viewport such as `30.1,-97.9|30.4,` passes this check and is forwarded to Google instead of being dropped as the function's contract says. Reject empty coordinate components before converting them to numbers.

This new public proxy path has no deadline around the upstream fetch and buffers `response.json()` without a response-size cap. A stalled request or a chunked/oversized upstream body can therefore hold a handler indefinitely or grow process memory; the repository's proxy hardening requires both bounds. Add an `AbortSignal` timeout that remains active through body consumption and read the body through `readResponseJsonCapped` (with a fixed limit) before parsing.

This catch sends the raw upstream exception message to the browser. Network, URL, or runtime errors can disclose internal implementation details, contrary to the repository's sanitized-error boundary; return the fixed public failure message here, as the existing proxy policy requires.

Fixed in 771c9e5: blank components are rejected before `Number()` sees them, so `30.1,-97.9|30.4,` is dropped rather than read as the equator. Covered by three new cases in `src/googleGeocodeProxy.test.mjs`.

_🤖 Addressed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_

Fixed in 771c9e5: the upstream call carries an `AbortSignal.timeout` of 10s, and the same signal is passed through `readResponseJsonCapped` at a 256 KiB ceiling, so the deadline stays armed during body consumption. An oversized body now answers 502 instead of borrowing the upstream status. Covered by a new test.

_🤖 Addressed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_

Fixed in 771c9e5: the catch no longer reads the exception and returns the fixed `Google Geocoding request failed` text. A new test asserts a `connect ECONNREFUSED 10.0.0.7:443` never reaches the browser.

_🤖 Addressed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_
The inline comment has a grammatical error: “which read as a hardening failure” should be phrased as “which was treated as a hardening failure” (or similar) to avoid ambiguity.

This request carries `x-api-key`, but `fetch` follows redirects by default. A provider-side redirect could send the credential-bearing request to an off-origin host and violates the repository's fixed-upstream proxy policy; reject redirects here (as the other providers do) or validate every hop explicitly.

The daily-budget admission check runs once before `refresh()`, but this loop continues to call `upstream()` for every remaining page without rechecking the governor. After an early page crosses the cap, the default refresh can still spend all remaining pages (and an unmeasured 100-result refresh can charge roughly 12 points per page), defeating the stated daily point limit. Check/reserve the budget before each page and stop with a budget-blocked partial result when it is exhausted.

This issue also appears on line 686 of the same file.

The hourly view cap is checked before an asynchronous upstream call and the slot is recorded only after success. Concurrent requests can all observe the same counter and pass, while failed upstream attempts consume no slot, allowing retries to exceed the advertised cap. Reserve the slot immediately after the admission check, before awaiting `upstream`, so every admitted attempt counts.

The radius is computed from the original viewport and then the center is snapped by up to 0.25° per axis, but the radius is not widened after that shift. The existing tight Moscow case moves the requested center about 28 km from the camera target while retaining a 25 km radius, so the NEWS IN VIEW circle can exclude the very view it is supposed to cover. Compute coverage from the snapped center (or promote to the next accepted radius) before building this descriptor.

A stale proxy response carries the original `fetchedAt`, but this code re-dates its articles to `clock()` before retaining them. During an upstream outage the server can return the same cached batch as stale for nearly the rest of its one-hour window; each ten-minute browser refresh then grants that batch another hour on the map, allowing provider data to survive for almost two hours. Retain batches against the source fetch time (while handling clock skew explicitly) and avoid admitting a stale response as a newly fetched batch.

This newly clickable card only sets `interactive` and `url`; it does not provide an `accessibilityLabel`/`activate` action, and `createTrackedOverlayEntry` does not derive those fields from the URL. The overlay's keyboard-accessible mirror explicitly filters out entries without both fields, so keyboard and assistive-technology users cannot open the same article that pointer users can. Add an accessible activation action and propagate it through the tracked-readout bridge.

The data-source description says the browser receives “no ... images,” but the new `WORLD_NEWS_THUMBNAILS` setting deliberately sends HTTPS publisher image URLs to the browser. Qualify this as “no images by default” (or otherwise state the opt-in exception) so this required disclosure accurately describes the runtime contract.

This documents the no-header fallback as `1 point + 0.01 per result`, but `estimateWorldNewsPoints()` defaults to `withEntities=true` and charges `1 + 0.11 * resultCount` because every proxy request sets `add-entities=true`. A 100-result unmeasured response is therefore estimated at 12 points, not 2; the same stale rate is also repeated in DATA_SOURCES and the provider comments. Correct the documented fallback so operators do not size the daily budget against a six-times-too-low cost.

This proxy documentation says the no-header fallback is the `1 + 0.01 per result` estimate, but every request sets `add-entities=true` and `estimateWorldNewsPoints()` charges the entity-bearing `1 + 0.11 per result` rate. Align this description and the related budget copy with the actual charge, otherwise operators may underestimate spend when quota headers are absent.

The standalone server sends requests to unauthenticated, credential-backed `/api/*` routes without checking the request `Host`. Unlike Vite's restricted `allowedHosts` setting (`build/vite.js:31-37`), listening on `127.0.0.1` alone does not protect against a hostile hostname resolving to loopback. Validate the Host before routing, reject unexpected names, and explicitly configure any intended remote or reverse-proxy hosts; add a request-level regression test.

The mount matches `/healthz` and every nested path, and this handler ignores the method, so `POST /healthz` and `GET /healthz/anything` both return a misleading healthy `200` even though the contract specifies only `GET /healthz`. Check the rewritten path and method; let unknown paths fall through and reject unsupported methods with `405`.

`httpServer.close()` waits for active responses, so a long-lived CCTV media response can keep `SIGTERM` shutdown pending without a limit. The CCTV puller and AIS watchdog also listen for the server's `close` event, delaying their cleanup until the connection ends. Stop accepting requests, allow a bounded drain, then terminate remaining connections and run provider teardown so the process exits reliably.

When the port is occupied or the configured host cannot bind, `listen()` emits `error` instead of invoking this callback. With no listener, the process crashes and providers initialized by `createHeadlessApiApp()` are not torn down. Reject the startup promise on a listen error, call `app.close()`, and preserve the original error for the caller.

This release note, `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md:940-941`, and the PR description say the reference covers every exposed endpoint, but its Scope and §7 explicitly limit coverage to selected routes; mounted APIs such as CCTV media and AIS are missing. Change these claims to say it documents a selected subset, or extend the reference to cover the remaining routes. The reference's stated limited scope is otherwise clear.

This blanket `no-store` contract is incorrect for live transit snapshots: `transitResponseHeaders` sets `Cache-Control: public, max-age=15` for fresh data (`src/data/transitProxy.js:294-300`). Clients relying on this text may assume every poll reaches the server and mishandle freshness.

The OpenSky proxy also passes through unsuccessful upstream statuses (including 401/403 auth failures) and returns 502 on an uncached proxy error when regional fallback is unavailable (`server/providers/aircraft/opensky.js:561-595,638-647,683-692`). This section currently lists only 200 and 429, leaving consumers without the actual authentication and failure contract.

`X-Transit-Contact` is emitted from `Math.floor(contactedAt)`, where `contactedAt` comes from `Date.now()` (`src/data/transitProxy.js:306-307`); it is epoch **milliseconds**, not seconds. Consumers following this contract will calculate an incorrect age for a revalidated feed.

The first failed transit upstream request with no cached snapshot is not necessarily `503`. `src/sources/transitService.js:374-393` returns `502` for upstream status, oversized body, or unsupported feed shape, and `504` for other fetch failures; `503` is the cooldown or admission path. Document the distinctions so clients can interpret retries correctly.

Fixed in e358c72: requests are now rejected with 403 before routing unless `Host` is an IP literal, `localhost`/`*.localhost`, the bind host, or listed in `GEV_HEADLESS_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, mirroring Vite's own host check. This includes a request-level regression test against a real listening server, showing that a rejected request never reaches a provider.
Fixed in 4f798d4: only an exact `GET`/`HEAD /healthz` is answered. Other methods get `405` with `Allow: GET, HEAD`, and nested paths fall through to the router's `404`.

Fixed in 4f798d4: `close()` now closes idle connections immediately, gives in-flight responses a grace period (`GEV_HEADLESS_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_MS`, default 5 s), then force-closes the rest, so the providers' `close` listeners and plugin teardown run promptly. Verified live: with a connection held open, the process exited 5.1 s after `SIGTERM`, instead of waiting for the 60 s header timeout.

Fixed in 4f798d4: a listen error now rejects the startup promise after `app.close()` tears down the already-initialized providers. The original error is preserved, and the entrypoint exits 1 with the reason (verified live with a port already in use).

Fixed in 0566c67: the CHANGELOG, CURRENT-STATE and the reference itself now say it covers a selected subset, and point to `server/apiRoutes.js` (from #793) as the complete mount list. I updated the PR description too.
Fixed in 0566c67: the convention is now per-endpoint, and the transit section documents `public, max-age=15` for fresh snapshots, with `no-store` only on `STALE-ERROR` and error responses.

Fixed in 0566c67: the reference now documents that other non-2xx upstream statuses pass through when neither the cache nor the regional fallback can serve, the auth-specific `401`/`403` bodies and their `X-OpenSky-Auth-Reason` values, and the `502` on an uncached proxy error.
Correct. I fixed the docs in 0566c67 to say epoch milliseconds, which is what the code emits, and left the header itself unchanged, because the browser client already consumes it as milliseconds.

Fixed in 0566c67: the reference now distinguishes `502` (the operator answered badly: an error status, an oversized body, or a differential feed), `504` (other fetch failures), and `503` (a retry cooldown, or the provider shutting down), plus the `200 STALE-ERROR` response when a cached snapshot exists.

**P1 — performance/scope:** the second surface changes from 640 px at 15 fps to 1280 px at 60 fps. At equal aspect ratio that's up to **16× the drawn pixels per second** for a fast source, independent of the unrelated CCTV docking fix. This may penalize the constrained GPUs targeted by GEV. Could we keep the existing 640/15 defaults for this PR, or isolate the higher-quality mode behind an explicit setting and provide measured p95 frame time/CPU cost on representative hardware? The new test checks the new limit, not its performance impact.

`index.html` already contains the `provider-settings` template marker at line 33, and `build/application-html.js` expands it to `src/ui/templates/provider-settings.html`. This second inline block therefore creates duplicate `#key-setup-chip` and `#key-setup` IDs in the built page; `initKeySetup` initializes only the first matching surface, leaving the duplicate stale. Remove this inline block and keep the template marker as the single source of the POWER UP markup.

`StyleManager` has no `_formatCount` method (and this class no longer extends one that provides it). As soon as the manager supplies any health row, opening/refreshing the panel throws `TypeError: this._formatCount is not a function`, so the provider list cannot render. Use a local formatter or an existing number-formatting utility here.

`buildProviderHealthRows` computes `row.updated`, but this rendering path never uses it. When a provider has cached records plus an error (or another detail string), `row.detail` wins over the age in `providerHealth.js`, so the health panel omits the required last-update time exactly in the degraded/stale cases where it is most useful. Render the update age separately, avoiding a duplicate when `row.detail` already contains it.

The retry value is rendered only when `_renderProviderHealth()` runs, but this panel has no timer; while it remains open, a `retry 60s` label never changes as time passes and only updates after a click or unrelated manager notification. Add a lightweight countdown tick while the popover is open and clear it during disposal/close.

This change replaces the compatibility entry with a second, legacy `StyleManager` implementation, but the running application still constructs `StyleManager` from `src/ui/composition.js` (`src/app/controls.js:2`), which extends `src/ui/applicationShell.js`. As a result, the provider-health initialization and data-manager subscription added here are never reached in the actual app. Keep this entrypoint as the compatibility re-export and wire the feature into the composed application shell/its owner instead.

The provider-health controller only binds existing `#provider-health-toggle`, `#provider-health-panel`, and `#provider-health-list` elements, but this markup still contains only the layer-toggle container here and no such elements are added in the referenced templates. `_initProviderHealthPanel()` therefore returns immediately, so the advertised health button/popover and all refresh logic are never visible. Add the health markup to the appropriate application template (and keep the `index.html` marker expansion as the source of truth).

`keyRequired` is calculated only after `state` is classified, so a key-gated layer is still exposed as `nominal`, `degraded`, or `unavailable` depending on its cached data/error. The render path merely overrides the visible text, leaving the row's `health-*` class, summary counts, and `buildProviderHealthRows()` API inconsistent with the required distinct KEY REQUIRED state. Classify key-required rows before `layerFeedState` and add a dedicated label/style (or otherwise make all consumers use the same state).

`_initProviderHealthPanel()` is invoked here, but the assembled markup still does not define `#provider-health-toggle` or `#provider-health-panel` (`src/ui/templates/provider-settings.html` only contains the key-setup UI). The guard in that initializer therefore returns immediately, so the advertised SYSTEM HEALTH button/popover and all rendered rows are never visible. Add the health controls/list to an application template (and ensure it is expanded into `index.html`) before relying on this wiring.

The summary treats `fallback` as live and omits every other non-nominal state such as `loading` and `partial`. For example, an ADS-B fallback row will show `1 live · 0 attention` even though its row is explicitly labeled FALLBACK, which makes the summary misleading. Count only `nominal` as live and count non-`off`, non-`nominal` rows as attention.

The existing template markers above still expand `display-controls`, `command-dock`, `layer-panels`, `context`, and `welcome`, but this added block is already-expanded markup for those templates and replaces the `hud-loading` marker. `expandApplicationHtml()` will therefore emit duplicate element IDs (and the application HTML test fails); keep only the `hud-loading` template marker here.

This changes the documented compatibility entrypoint from the standalone wrapper to the composed class. A direct `new StyleManager(viewer)` now reaches `src/ui/composition.js` with `services` undefined, and `applicationShell.js` immediately destructures that value, so legacy direct construction throws before the UI is usable. Please retain the standalone catalog/service defaults here and keep the composed class for normal application assembly.

The new `monitor_heart` ligature is not present in the `icon_names` subset requested by `index.html`. The repository's glyph check will flag this, and the browser will render the literal `monitor_heart` text instead of the health icon; add the glyph to the subset when introducing it here.

The real layer manager publishes status changes from `refreshLayerStats()` and periodic data updates through `subscribeActivity()`, not only through `subscribe()`. Listening to `subscribe()` leaves this panel's summary and rows stale for out-of-band updates such as Transit and Directions, contrary to the automatic-refresh requirement. Prefer `subscribeActivity` here, with `subscribe` only as a compatibility fallback.

`documentRef` is injected into this class, but this render path calls the global `document` instead. A headless/embedded caller that supplies a fake document (the constructor's stated seam) will throw before rendering the summary; retain the reference and use it for all `createTextNode`/`createElement` calls.

This new module only needs the pure `layerFeedState` helper, but importing `data/manager.js` pulls in the lifecycle and presentation compatibility facade. That creates unnecessary coupling and initialization for a UI snapshot helper; import `./data/feedState.js` directly, as the layer panel does.

Resolved in 37ff695 (merge resolution): `index.html` now keeps only the `gev:template hud-loading` marker — the expanded pp-toggles/command-dock markup lives in the component templates, so `expandApplicationHtml()` emits every element once. The application-HTML test (`the standalone document expands every component once and preserves unique element ids`) passes.

Resolved in 37ff695: `src/ui.js` is restored as the standalone `StyleManager` wrapper, byte-identical to `main`, injecting `catalogControlServices(getStandaloneCatalog())` plus the standalone surface services as defaults so direct `new StyleManager(viewer)` construction works. Application assembly is unchanged — `src/app/controls.js` imports the composed class from `ui/composition.js`.

**P1 — the `view` stage is checked only once, before the awaits.** Cockpit / Clean View / recording / scene playback are checked here, but the map switch (~L3641), the layer enable and `openNearest` (~L3726) all await after it. If the user presses Clean View or enters cockpit while Google 3D loads, the turn is still current, so the panorama loads in the hidden panel, the action returns `ok: true` and the reply says it is showing. That billed, unseen load is exactly what this stage exists to stop. Reproduced with a probe test: Clean View switched on during the layer enable still gave `ok: true`, `open:google:250` and a reveal-panel call. Suggest re-checking after each await, and checking the hiding classes again right before `openNearest` and the reveal.

**P1 — a navigation after arrival does not invalidate the remaining stages.** `current()` checks the turn's lifetime, not who owns the camera. Scenario: the street-level flight lands, then the user searches or flies elsewhere while Google 3D loads; the old request still lights its provider and opens or arms imagery for the previous destination. Suggest capturing the navigation generation when the flight lands and refusing the later stages once it moves on (the same idea links use in `embed.js`, but checked after each await).

Same gap for links: `navigatedSince` is checked only before the action runs. If the user pans while the map switches, a Mapillary / KartaView / Panoramax link still opens its photo at the link's point (with `frame: false`) while the user is elsewhere. Google only arms and has the 1 km reach check, so it is the free sources that misbehave here.

**P2 — the previous photo stays open on an empty result.** The failure paths here (~L3746–3786) set the error but never call `closeViewer`, and `openNearest` only sets an error too. Scenario: "Eiffel Tower on Mapillary" opens a photo, then "Sahara on Mapillary" flies to the Sahara and says there is no imagery, but the Paris photo is still on screen next to the error. `applyView` already closes the old photo; this path should match.
Same as above for `openLinkedStreetLevel`: pasting an `sl=` link that finds nothing into an open tab leaves the previous photo up.

**P3 — the camera flies before the `view` stage can refuse.** During recording or scene playback, "show me X on Street View" first flies the camera away from the recording or scene, then says the panel is hidden. The `view` check does not depend on the location, so it can run before the flight.

**P3 — a passed-through view keeps its old photo point when only the camera changes.** An `area` moves the `street_level` point, a new `camera` does not. Passing a Paris view that has `street_level` with `camera` set to New York yields `sl` at Paris, and the app flies to Paris, ignoring the camera.

**P3 —** the doc says `revealPanel` "does nothing above 720px", but `scrollIntoView` runs on desktop too. Since `streetLevelControls.js:404` now calls it on every photo open (ground clicks included), the rail scrolls on desktop.

**The wait for the floor has no time limit, and the view shows nothing while it waits.**

Inputs: a provider whose first frame has `heightM: null`, at a place where the floor cell never warms. That happens when the terrain proxy fails, for example: `cachedGroundFloor` then stays null.

Wrong result:

- Every update returns here, so `placeCamera` never runs.
- The HUD stays on the entry frame, because subject HUD updates happen only inside `placeCamera`.
- Nothing on screen says the view is acquiring: `updateSubjectHud` never reads `surfaceAcquiring`.

The user is in an entered Cockpit that never moves. The comment says this works "as the built-in views wait for the surface", but the aircraft path caps its wait at `COCKPIT_GROUND_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS` and then sets `surfaceFallback`.

Fix:

- Bound this wait the same way, with `cockpitSurfaceWaitExpired(…, COCKPIT_GROUND_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS)`. After it, fall back to a stated height with `surfaceFallback = true`, or end the view.
- Keep the HUD updating while waiting, and show the acquiring and fallback state.
- Update the matching CURRENT-STATE sentence.

**`selectedAtMs` can report another train's selection time.**

`_selectedAtMs` is stamped only in `selectAndFocusTrain`, and `clearSelection` never clears it.

Inputs:

1. Select train A (stamped t1).
2. Press Escape.
3. A provider holds train B: `setCockpitSubject(B)` selects through `selectTrain`, which doesn't stamp.

Wrong result: B's snapshot reports t1, A's time, against the documented "null for any other".

Transit stamps on its `setCockpitSubject` path, so the two layers disagree on whether a hold counts as a selection.

Fix:

- Reset `_selectedAtMs` in `clearSelection`.
- Stamp it, or set it to null, when `setCockpitSubject` selects a train that wasn't selected.
- Match Transit's choice, and word the docs to agree.

Fixed in 4c335521. The wait for the floor is now bounded by `COCKPIT_GROUND_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS` (5 s), as the aircraft path's is. While it waits, the HUD keeps updating and reads ACQUIRING SURFACE. After the timeout the view ends and the provider gets `release(id, {restore:false})`: a subject that never had a height has nothing honest to fall back to, unlike an aircraft with its own reported altitude. Mid-ride, a frame with no height keeps the last height. CURRENT-STATE and APPLICATION.md say so. Tests: a floor that never comes ends the view after the wait, with the camera never placed.

Fixed in 4c335521. A hold that returns a promise is still refused at once, and is now released again once that promise settles, unless that same subject is being ridden by then. `release` must tolerate a second call, which the docs now state; Rail and Transit already do, and a test covers calling it twice. Test: an asynchronous hold that lands after entry was refused is released again.

Fixed in 4c335521. A hold never counts as the user's selection, in Rail and Transit alike: `selectedAtMs` is stamped only by a click, `focusTrain` or `focusVehicle`; `clearSelection` resets it; and a train or vehicle selected only by a hold reads null. Transit no longer stamps on its hold path. The rule is stated in both headers, CURRENT-STATE and APPLICATION.md, with tests in both layers.
